title: BlackRock’s Larry Fink Warns AI Data Center Halt Could Tip US Into Recession - Decrypt
text:
BlackRock CEO Larry Fink has a blunt warning about what could derail the U.S. economy: slamming the brakes on the data centers powering the AI boom.
Speaking to CNBC on Wednesday after BlackRock posted better-than-expected third-quarter earnings, Fink said the surge in AI infrastructure spending has become so central to economic growth that choking it off would be dangerous.
“If we have a moratorium of some sort in this country, we will be in a recession,” he said, adding that “so much of our economy is based on the build-out of this capex.”
The comments come as data centers have become a flashpoint ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, with local opposition mounting over their electricity demands, water use and strain on power grids.
According to Brookings, at least 100 localities had approved moratoriums by July, and New York has paused certain permits for up to a year. Fink pushed back on the backlash, calling much of it “misinformation” and insisting that “data centers are not the problem,” pointing instead to the construction jobs and energy-infrastructure demand the buildout is generating.
The scale of the spending underscores his argument. Wall Street analysts estimate AI capital expenditures could top $1 trillion in 2027 and exceed $5 trillion cumulatively through 2030, making the sector a meaningful driver of the roughly 3% annualized GDP growth Fink wants to sustain. He has argued more private capital is needed to keep it going, and said BlackRock has spoken with chipmakers including AMD and Broadcom about the effort.
But Fink is swimming against a sharply rising tide of public opposition. An Annenberg Public Policy Center survey this summer found 61% of Americans oppose new data centers in their area, up from 49% in the spring, with majorities of Democrats, Republicans and independents all against them.
The concerns center on soaring electricity demand, water use and strain on local grids. That backlash has already produced real restrictions: New York has a moratorium on hyperscale data centers, Texas has paused approvals, and cities from Austin to Jersey City have imposed limits, with Data Center Watch counting roughly $130 billion in projects blocked or delayed in the first quarter of 2026 alone.
It has also become a live electoral issue. The fight is central to Ohio’s Senate race, where Democrat Sherrod Brown has campaigned against the buildout, and a super PAC backed by AI billionaires including Marc Andreessen and OpenAI President Greg Brockman has poured millions into ads defending data centers across battleground states. President Donald Trump has weighed in too, warning that communities resisting the facilities risk ending up “backwards and poor.”
Against that backdrop, Fink pushed back directly, suggesting the AI buildout in the United States is propping up the U.S. economy and any shift would result in a significant downturn.
The warning carries weight for crypto, given how closely Bitcoin now tracks broader risk sentiment and macro conditions.
Fink, who runs the world’s largest asset manager and oversees its dominant spot Bitcoin ETF, has become one of Wall Street’s most prominent crypto converts. He has called Bitcoin an asset for a “frightened world” and framed it as a legitimate alternative investment, while BlackRock has flagged AI agents as a potential next wave of crypto demand.

title: Google Says AI Isn't Building Itself Yet—Even Though It Writes 75% of the Code - Decrypt
text:
Google DeepMind went looking for proof that AI is speeding up the development of AI itself. It didn’t find any.
In the safety report for Gemini 4 Argon, its most powerful model, the lab concluded AI research isn’t moving any faster, even though AI now writes most of the code DeepMind’s engineers ship.
The finding cuts against the scenario that has spooked AI executives into calling for a slowdown. It’s called recursive self-improvement: an AI builds a smarter version of itself, which builds an even smarter one, until progress outruns anyone’s ability to test, regulate, or switch it off—what the report calls “a situation where existing guardrails are severely inadequate.”
“There is currently no significant end-to-end acceleration of ML R&D, AI-driven or otherwise,” Haydn Belfield, a Google DeepMind researcher who worked on the assessment, wrote in a thread on X. “We therefore conclude that the risk from AI-driven ML R&D is currently low.”
ML R&D is shorthand for machine learning research and development, the work of building new AI models.
1/9 In the Gemini 4 Argon Safety & Security Report, we published our first holistic empirical assessment of ML R&D automation and acceleration inside Google DeepMind — combining capability benchmarks, a macro capability index, data on AI-written code and trajectory outcomes, and… pic.twitter.com/Vr8Q5Obbsp
— Haydn Belfield (@HaydnBelfield) October 14, 2026
DeepMind tracks the issue because “AI could speed up frontier capability gains faster than safety, governance, and societal adaptation can keep pace,” Belfield wrote. More automation also means giving AI agents broader access to company systems, more room for a misaligned model (one pursuing goals its makers never intended) to cause trouble.
To measure progress, the team built GCI v1, an internal index that blends the scores of 123 AI models across 92 benchmarks into a single number per model—think of it as an IQ score for AI. “Frontier Gemini capabilities have improved at a remarkably steady pace of ~0.1 GCI points/month,” Belfield wrote.
In the report’s chart of that index, Gemini 1.5 Pro sits near 0.5 points in late 2024 and Gemini 3.8 Flash just above 2.9 in September 2026, with nearly every release hugging a straight line. Argon is the one dot poking above it, at roughly 3.3, though its error bar (the range its true score could plausibly fall in) stretches low enough to touch the trend.
“While Gemini 4 Argon sits above [the] trend, we trace this to increased compute and organizational investment rather than reflecting AI-driven acceleration,” Belfield wrote. Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon on September 30.
Most production code at DeepMind is now more than 75% AI-written, and the share of fully delegated pull requests (bundles of code changes submitted for review before they go live) rose from 7.5% to 11.9% between April and September. But “~88% of pull requests still require multi-turn human steering or human code authorship—and code changes remain subject to human review before submission,” Belfield wrote.
A survey of 12 senior DeepMind leaders and researchers found automation is highest in “well-specified, verifiable execution tasks and lowest in open-ended scientific ideation, novel experimental design, diagnosing subtle training instabilities, and long-horizon research taste.” In plain terms, AI is great at executing instructions and bad at deciding which ideas are worth chasing.
DeepMind also reviewed 1,389 logs of Argon working as an agent inside the company. The bigger the task, the less likely the model finished it alone and the more often a human stepped in.
The report landed a month after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei argued that recursive self-improvement is already accelerating, a warning Sam Altman and Elon Musk endorsed and one that sent chip stocks down almost 6%. Days earlier, former Anthropic engineer Jacob Coxon had quit the industry, warning AI could “kill us all by the end of the decade.”
DeepMind’s numbers cover only its own lab, and the same report says it can’t rule out that an unrestricted Argon crosses its danger thresholds for cyberattacks and bioweapons information.

title: Mastercard and BVNK Launch 'Global Money Platform' to Merge Fiat and Stablecoins - Decrypt
text:
Mastercard is folding stablecoins into its sprawling payments empire, launching a platform that lets businesses hold, move, and spend traditional currencies and digital dollars side by side through a single connection.
Unveiled Thursday, the Mastercard Global Money Platform pairs the payments giant’s global network with the stablecoin infrastructure of BVNK, the crypto firm Mastercard acquired in August.
Mastercard struck the deal to buy BVNK for roughly $1.8 billion, and the new platform marks the first major integration of the two companies’ capabilities since that acquisition closed.
At the center of the platform is what Mastercard calls a global money account, a multi-currency account where fiat and stablecoins can sit together, with conversion between them handled through a single API.
Banks, fintechs and enterprises can embed those accounts into their own branded products, along with real-time conversion, stablecoin-linked cards and local bank payouts, or use the platform to run their own treasury and settlement. The pitch is a modular toolkit spanning sending, receiving, converting, storing, spending and earning, letting customers start with the pieces they need and bolt on more over time.
Mastercard framed the offering as plumbing for a “multi-money” world. The platform ties into Mastercard Move, the company’s money-transfer network, letting users tap stablecoin balances to send local-currency payments into recipients’ bank accounts, with coverage expected to reach more than 40 currencies across 200-plus countries in 2027. Customers will also be able to spend stablecoin balances across Mastercard’s merchant-acceptance network, with card issuing available in more than 130 countries.
Payments firm Nuvei and card-issuing platform Marqeta are among the first to integrate the platform, alongside Ontop, Beem, and Almond FinTech.
Raj Dhamodharan, Mastercard’s executive vice president for blockchain and digital assets, said the company believes “the future of commerce will be built on interoperability across multiple forms of money,” calling the launch a step toward enabling “the next generation of programmable and agentic commerce.”
That nod to agentic commerce, where AI agents transact on their own, signals where Mastercard sees the puck heading.
The company has already moved to enable AI-agent payments alongside crypto heavyweights like Coinbase and Ripple, and secured a New York BitLicense covering stablecoins and tokenized deposits. Mastercard said Global Money Platform will add support for agentic commerce and tokenized deposits down the line.

title: Bitcoin Whipsaws as Crypto Liquidations Near $1 Billion - Decrypt
text:
Bitcoin fell below $80,000 on Thursday for the first time in over a month, extending Wednesday’s inflation-driven slide and wiping out nearly $1 billion in leveraged crypto bets. It's currently trading just about $82,000 after several hours of increased volatility.
Ethereum and XRP dropped close to 5%, Zcash sank almost 10%, and only five coins in the top 100 managed gains above 1%. Pick any coin in the top 100 and it's likely in the red today.
Across the market, 177,440 traders were liquidated in 24 hours for a total of $948.22 million, per CoinGlass, with longs accounting for $858.96 million, or 90.6%. Ethereum led with $282.03 million, with Bitcoin just behind at a little over $200 million.
This was the third-heaviest day for long liquidations in the last 90 days, behind October 8 and August 22. The largest single order liquidated yesterday was a $12.03 million Bitcoin long on Binance, force-closed at $80,208.96.
A liquidation happens when a trader borrows to bet on a price move and the market goes the other way. Once losses eat through the collateral, the exchange sells the position automatically, and that forced selling drags prices lower and trips the next batch of leveraged longs.
The trigger was Wednesday’s inflation report, which showed consumer prices up 3.7% year over year in September against a 3.6% forecast, with core inflation at 2.6% against 2.5%. Thursday’s Producer Price Index, which tracks business input costs, rose 6.3% annually versus a 5.5% forecast.
Much of that inflation comes from oil, with Brent crude near $104 a barrel, about 70% above a year ago amid the war between the U.S. and Iran. That feeds into fuel, shipping, and almost everything else that needs to be transported to reach consumers.
Hot inflation pushes the Federal Reserve toward higher interest rates, which lifts Treasury yields, the return investors earn for lending to the U.S. government. A bond paying around 5% with almost no risk makes Bitcoin a harder sell, while higher rates make borrowing pricier and strengthen the dollar, draining the cheap money leveraged crypto traders run on.
Iliya Kalchev, analyst at Nexo, reads the selloff as a broad exit from risk more than a Fed story, with stocks and copper falling, gold rising and South Korea’s Kospi down about 8%.
“Bitcoin has slipped to the bottom of the $81,000 to $87,000 range it has held since late September, and Glassnode flags $80,000 as the level to watch,” Kalchev told Decrypt. “It is also now roughly 2% below the average cost of U.S. spot ETF holders, near $82,300, after closing above that line on 21 of the 24 days since September 21. That puts ETF buyers back underwater, and reclaiming it is the first test of any rebound,”
On the daily chart, Bitcoin broke below $81,603, the strongest upper support from its August-to-October rally from $62,763 to $87,422, where uptrend pullbacks often stall. The drop reached $79,711 before buyers pulled the price back near $80,925, off a rising trend band near $80,286.
The Relative Strength Index, a 0-to-100 momentum gauge where 50 splits bulls from bears, fell to about 44, while the golden cross still keeps the longer-term uptrend intact.
A daily close back above $81,603 would reopen the path to $84,245 and the $87,422 swing high. Losing $80,286 would expose $78,002 as the next support, and then $75,092.
Kalchev sees early signs the selling is not deepening, including cooling profit-taking, but said a recovery needs more than a bounce.
“Three things need to line up for Bitcoin to push through. ETF flows have to turn consistently positive, after $681 million of outflows last week and a single $177 million inflow day. Selling by long-term holders has to ease,” Kalchev explained.
For Kalchev, a bullish market would require that leverage happens with a sustained buying instead of just a bounce. He added that a “Fed path that stops at one 25 basis point hike would take some pressure off the backdrop.”
The Fed announces its rate decision on October 28, followed by core PCE inflation data the next day and October payrolls on November 6.

title: Ethereum, Altcoins See 'Outsized Drawdowns' Due to Macro Pressures - Decrypt
text:
Altcoins have taken a hit over the past 24 hours, with major tokens seeing "outsized drawdowns" compared to Bitcoin. Experts say that this has largely been prompted by macro pressures pushing prices down.
With the market cap of all cryptocurrencies dropping by 2.5% to $2.8 trillion, Ethereum dropped by 5.5% to a $289 billion market cap over the past 24 hours, XRP fell by 5.1% to $82.4 billion, and Solana slipped by 3.8% to $60.6 billion. Meanwhile, industry leader Bitcoin has slipped by 3.1% on the day and 2.6% on the week, sitting at a market cap of $1.6 trillion.
It comes after the consumer price index rose 3.7% in the year to September, as Decrypt reported on Wednesday, with Myriad predictors pointing to a 28% chance of an October interest rate hike (Disclaimer: Myriad is a prediction market operated by Decrypt's parent company Dastan).
Nick Forster, founder of options trading exchange Derive.xyz, said in a note shared with Decrypt that this shifted traders into "protection mode" as "hedging activity" on the platform doubled, and whales pulled back on optimistic bets made in spring.
"This immediate pull-back from long-term upside bets alongside aggressive short-term hedging shows a dramatic regime shift," he said, "with institutional participants rapidly reassessing their macro risk exposure as the path for interest rates turns murky again."
When markets react like this, Luke Nolan, senior research associate at CoinShares, says that altcoins are impacted the most.
"[It] seems to be high beta assets just got hit harder, similar to in equities as well, where the high flyers have seen outsized drawdowns in recent sessions," Nolan told Decrypt. "Alts are typically more sensitive to financial conditions, and tightening affects the premise of liquidity expanding."
Nolan also highlighted the U.S. dollar hitting a near 18-month high as a downward pressure on the entire crypto market. He said that over a medium-term horizon, crypto tends to have an inverse correlation to the US Dollar Index, or DXY. This is partly due to crypto being priced in dollars, Nolan explained, but also because a rising dollar causes a tightening in liquidity and a fall in risk appetite.
Max Shannon, senior associate at Bitwise Europe, told Decrypt that the slide is also a hangover from altcoins’ “strength and momentum” over recent months.
Since the start of October, futures open interest in altcoins (excluding Ethereum) has fallen by $8 billion, Shannon said. To him, that shows traders have “taken chips off the table,” which is a natural reaction after such a strong run.
That pattern is playing out with Ethereum, he added. ETH outperformed Bitcoin for three consecutive months, the first time it’s managed that since March 2021, and investors have been cashing in since. Ethereum ETFs saw 11 straight trading days of net outflows totalling $782.8 million, he said, before a brief inflow on Tuesday. Money has been heading back out since, per CoinGlass data, with $129.5 million in net outflows.
"This price action is more of a consolidation period for altcoins that have already done well," Shannon told Decrypt. "Altcoins generally tend to exhibit high correlations with BTC in tough times and lower correlations, especially with idiosyncratic catalysts, in better market environments. Hence, for the near term, it is possible that these altcoins trade in lockstep with BTC, albeit more sensitively."
For prices to recover, Nolan says he wants to see expectations of an interest rate hike in October to fall. Right now, he struggles to call a bottom for altcoins as he sees valid arguments for movements in either direction.
"I could see a situation where Bitcoin loses its support and altcoins likely bleed further," Nolan told Decrypt. "The opposite could also be true: this could be just a short-term correction, and we could be back into decent market conditions soon, which if Bitcoin was to push back decently above 80k, I could very well see an outsized up move for altcoins."

title: Ledger Announces Atom Touchscreen Android Device - Decrypt
text:
Ledger's new Atom device will ship with Solana's Seeker app preinstalled, the companies announced on stage at Ledger's Op3n conference in Paris on Thursday.
Billed as a "signer" rather than a hardware wallet, the Atom is an Android-powered touchscreen device equipped with a data-only eSIM and Ledger's Secure Element, enabling users to send and receive encrypted messages with other Atom users as well as perform crypto transactions in the manner of its range of wallets. To do so, the device switches into a Ledger OS-powered "Secure Mode" for sensitive operations such as signing transactions and authorising AI agent requests.
The Atom sports a 6.77-inch OLED display, rear camera and 4,000mAh battery, and runs on a Qualcomm Dragonwing chip. It also incorporates a hardware privacy switch that physically cuts power to the camera and microphone.
The device also runs third-party apps, and will come preinstalled with Solana's Seeker app after Solana Mobile named Ledger as its first hardware expansion partner. Seeker combines Solana Mobile's wallet with its Solana dapp Store, which lists more than 1,500 decentralized apps, and will appear on Atom's home screen. Until now, the store was available on Solana Mobile's own Seeker phone.
Your wealth is digital. The device you manage it with should be built for that.
Meet Ledger Atom™: the security of industry leading hardware, the convenience of your everyday apps, plus control over your AI tools, and a rapidly expanding platform of apps, all in one quantum… pic.twitter.com/vHhDNQYipz
— Ledger (@Ledger) October 15, 2026
Ledger Atom runs on the Android Open Source Project, the free, open version of Google's mobile operating system, alongside a Secure Element chip running Ledger OS. Its display and touch controls are physically isolated from Android, according to the release, and approvals in the Seeker app happen in a "Secure Mode" backed by the Secure Element.
"Having the Seeker app on Ledger Atom from day one just makes sense, so Ledger users get access to the Solana ecosystem without giving up any of the security," said Ian Rogers, Ledger's chief human agency officer.
Solana Mobile began opening its software stack to other Android manufacturers in March. Samsung Wallet also recently added USDC transfers on Solana. Seeker has handled more than $13 billion in transaction volume and 154 million transactions, according to the company, which says it has sold more than 200,000 devices across Seeker and its earlier Saga phone.
Hardware makers that integrate the stack can earn rewards in SKR, the native token of the Solana Mobile ecosystem, which also rewards users and developers, the release said.
Existing Seeker phones will remain fully supported, Solana Mobile said. Reservations for Ledger Atom are open now, though neither company has given a price or shipping date.
The Ledger Atom will include anti-tampering and tamper-evident features from the packaging to the device itself, according to the press release, including ways to help detect whether the enclosure has been opened, and will only be sold through Ledger's official site.
The announcement of the Atom comes at an awkward time for Ledger, as the firm investigates tampered devices in its reseller network linked to a suspected $87 million wallet drain.
The company this week disclosed that its Donjon security team had found an implant in a hardware wallet sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis that captures recovery phrases during setup and sends them out over LTE. On Tuesday, it asked resellers in six Southeast Asian countries and Hong Kong to pull its devices from shelves.

title: Zcash Tanks Double Digits After 'Meteoric Rise' Sees Leverage Build Up - Decrypt
text:
Privacy-focused cryptocurrency Zcash has fallen 11% over the past 24 hours to a market capitalization of $18.5 billion, per Decrypt data, making it one of the biggest losers of the day.
One expert says this drop in valuation comes after its price has soared in recent months, which has led to a build up in leverage and amplified losses. Others say that growing concerns that AI can break cryptography faster than quantum computers are causing the privacy token to take bigger losses.
Luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, highlighted that Zcash's "meteoric rise" means that it is still up 460% from its March lows and that in a "fragile" crypto market the largest gainers tend to take losses too.
"There was a decent build-up of leverage on the way up as this is also a natural consequence of a strong move," Nolan told Decrypt. "More attention brings more perp traders to take on leverage, and when there is a sneeze, the moves get amplified as those leveraged traders are either forced to reduce exposure or get liquidated."
Over the past 24 hours, per CoinGlass data, $17.9 million worth of Zcash long positions were liquidated, a large figure compared to Hyperliquid's $7.3 million over the same period.
The price drop comes as other industry-wide concerns start to swirl, some of which could see positive upside for Zcash.
Last week, Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin and Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake warned that the industry needs to plan for "bunker mode" as AI could break crypto encryption before quantum computers do. The conversation was sparked after OpenAI published major progress in math, which presented concerns for the future of encryption.
"The OpenAI math breakthroughs has caused a lot concern in crypto given the conspicuous lack of cryptography proofs," Ryan Zurrer, founder and director of investment firm Dialectic, told Decrypt. "More complex privacy protocols such as Zcash have the most to lose in a zero-day event if core primitives are rendered obsolete against AI-driven cryptography attacks."
Zcash has been aggressive with its quest to quantum-proof the network. Zakura, a Zcash full node developer, recently said that its team expects to be quantum-proofed as well as reasonably AI-proofed by January. Its quantum-resistant roadmap "served as a key catalyst" for its recent rally, Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey, told Decrypt. "Although actual implementation is still some distance away, it indeed reflects the market's continuous focus on the privacy sector since the beginning of this year."
Privacy continues to be a major crypto industry talking point. Sun added that as traditional finance continues to merge with the crypto industry, the need for privacy will continue to rise.
"As an increasing volume of traditional financial assets and operations migrate on-chain, privacy protection will no longer be merely an optional add-on," Sun told Decrypt, "but rather a fundamental prerequisite for financial institutions adopting blockchain technology."
Last week, French lawmakers progressed a law proposal that would require citizens to report crypto holdings equal to or above €100,000 ($112,000), or otherwise face a penalty. The proposed law received significant backlash in the wake of a wave of crypto-related "wrench attacks," robberies, and kidnappings across the country. Although the law hasn't passed yet, some have looked to privacy protocols as government oversight looms.
Nolan from CoinShares highlights that investors should zoom out when looking at Zcash's recent performance, pushing back on recent narratives pushing its price down.
"I think the French proposed law had little to do with the move, and in my view, it's simply a larger pullback given the meteoric rise," Nolan told Decrypt. "When you put the drawdown in context on the daily chart, even though it's been 35%+, it looks like a blip in comparison to the upmove."

title: Morning Minute: Solana Is About To Get Faster - Decrypt
text:
Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
Next Wednesday, Solana rips out the engine and drops in a new one while the car is doing 70 on the highway.
On October 21, around 15:00 UTC, Solana activates Alpenglow on mainnet, retiring the consensus mechanism it has run on since launch. Finality drops from roughly 12.8 seconds to a target of about 150 milliseconds – 85 times faster. Anza, the core dev shop behind it, called it “18 months of work for a migration that happens in one slot.”
Finality is the moment a transaction stops being reversible, the point where you can hand over the goods knowing the payment can’t be clawed back. Solana has always felt instant, but there was a roughly 13-second window where a block could in theory still get dropped. Every exchange and payment processor has had to build around that window. Next week it closes.
The old system breaks if more than about a third of staked SOL turns hostile. The new one is built to survive 20% of stake acting maliciously plus another 20% simply offline, and keep finalizing. For a chain whose reputation was built on outages, that’s the number institutions will actually care about.
Now the part that’s going to cause trouble. Validators currently cast their votes as transactions on the chain. Under Alpenglow they vote directly to each other instead, which means Solana’s headline transaction count and TPS figures are about to fall off a cliff. Nothing real changes - same users, same volume, same apps - but the number everyone has quoted for years was mostly validators voting at each other. Expect a wave of “Solana activity collapses” posts next Wednesday from people reading a dashboard.
This is also just phase one of two, and the second piece has no date yet. And Solana has missed an Alpenglow date before - a September 28 activation was announced, then pushed. So, grains of salt.
But clearly Solana is focused on speed as one of its primary differentiators - and it’s about to get a lot faster…

title: Bitcoin Tests $81,000 as Rate Hike Fears Linger After Hot Inflation Data - Decrypt
text:
Bitcoin dipped below $81,000 on Thursday, extending its slide a day after U.S. consumer prices rose faster than expected and revived bets on another Federal Reserve rate hike.
The leading cryptocurrency is currently trading at $81,002, per CoinGecko data, down 2.7% over the past 24 hours and 2.5% over the past week, after slipping to an intraday low of $80,444.
Consumer prices rose 3.7% in the year to September, Decrypt reported on Wednesday. Prices rose 0.6% over the month, the largest monthly increase in five months, driven mainly by energy costs tied to the war with Iran, The New York Times reported.
Traders' odds of a Fed rate hike this month jumped to 43% from 24% after the report, the Times said, though federal funds futures still point to December for the next increase. The Fed raised rates to a range of 3.75% to 4% in September.
CME FedWatch put the odds of an October hike at 29.3% on Thursday, up from 17.7% a week earlier, while traders on prediction markets Myriad and Polymarket priced it at 28%. Polymarket traders put the chance of a December hike at 79%. (Disclosure: Myriad is a prediction market operated by Decrypt's parent company, Dastan.)
Stephen Wundke, strategy and revenue director at quantitative investment firm Algoz, argued that those probabilities feed directly into Bitcoin's price. "On the bullish side as long as BTC stays above $79,500 we can keep the dream alive," Wundke told Decrypt.
Inflation has now run above the Fed's 2% target for 66 straight monthly readings, the longest streak this century, according to a CNBC analysis. "They're starting to accept high inflation as just a fact of life," Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack wrote in a LinkedIn post last week.
Those pressures are only part of the picture, Tim Sun of HashKey Group told Decrypt. Rising rate hike expectations, a stronger dollar and a pullback in AI tech stocks have weighed on Bitcoin on the surface, he said, "however, the deeper reason lies in the changing structure of incremental capital."
"Over the last two years, the key marginal buyers of Bitcoin primarily came from spot ETFs and corporate Bitcoin treasuries," Sun said. As borrowing costs rise, narrowing valuation premiums at some corporate treasuries have made it less attractive to raise money to keep buying Bitcoin, he added.
"Nevertheless, Bitcoin has not experienced a sustained deep sell-off as a result," Sun said, pointing to growing involvement from major traditional banks that has added long-term capital to the market.
Sun expects Bitcoin to stay range-bound in the short term. A breakout depends on whether ETF flows return to sustained net inflows and whether corporate treasuries can improve their ability to raise money and buy, he said.
Wundke also expects a range. "Without a clear catalyst to move things higher I fear we are range bound with BTC between $76,000 and $83,000 for the rest of October," he said, adding that peace with Iran "would change that dynamic instantly."
"In the short term Bitcoin trades as a liquidity asset, and higher for longer means tighter liquidity, so this drop is the market repricing rates, not a change in Bitcoin's story," Abdul Rafay Gadit, co-founder of ZIG Finance, told Decrypt.
"The next few weeks are about the Fed, not crypto," Gadit said. "If it signals it can look through sticky inflation, risk appetite returns quickly; if not, expect choppy trading."
The Fed will announce its next rate decision on October 28.

title: Brooklyn Prosecutors Take Down 112 Servers Behind Crypto Scam Targeting Russian Speakers - Decrypt
text:
Brooklyn prosecutors have dismantled the online infrastructure of a multinational crypto investment scam that targeted Russian speakers in the U.S., seizing and disrupting 241 web domains and 112 servers, District Attorney Eric Gonzalez announced on Wednesday.
The office's Virtual Currency Unit carried out search warrants and other enforcement actions across three time zones last week, working with the FBI. The servers were hosted by Eastern European and American companies, and the scammers relied on infrastructure and IP addresses in Ukraine and other Eastern European countries, according to the release.
"These criminals stole many millions of dollars from Russian-speaking victims through an elaborate investment scheme, then tried to exploit them again with false promises to recover their money," Gonzalez said.
A large cluster of victims in Brooklyn had each responded to a Russian-language Facebook ad for investment opportunities and then received a call from an "investment advisor" who coached them into opening an account on a crypto investment website, the office said.
With the advisor's help, victims bought crypto and sent it to addresses linked to the platforms. When they tried to withdraw after weeks or months of "investing," they were locked out or told to pay additional fees and taxes.
Data from the seized servers showed the scammers also ran a recovery scam, contacting victims a few weeks after the initial fraud and promising to get their stolen assets back, the DA's office said.
The unit had been investigating the operation for three years. Brooklyn's large Russian-speaking population meant the scam hit the borough's residents disproportionately, according to the release.
Before last week, the unit had already seized or disrupted 400 domains linked to the fraud, but new scam websites kept appearing. Taking down the servers removes the scammers' ability to quickly create new sites and contact existing victims, the office said.
Prosecutors estimate that tens of millions of dollars were stolen in the scheme. The office has seized about $300,000 so far and is working to claw back more.
The takedown is not the Brooklyn DA's only recent crypto fraud case. Its prosecutors previously charged a local man who stole $16 million from nearly 100 Coinbase users through a phishing scheme. He was sentenced to up to 12 years in prison.

title: Godfather of AI and 400 Scientists Want AI Models Cut Off From the Internet - Decrypt
text:
More than 400 scientists—including AI pioneers Geoffrey Hinton, known as the Godfather of AI, and Yoshua Bengio, who won the Turing Award in 2018—want the most dangerous AI models cut off from the internet.
An open letter published Tuesday asks AI labs to "airgap" cyber-capable models by default, which means physically disconnecting them from any outside network.
“In the short term, strong sandboxing mechanisms including airgapping (disconnecting from the internet) should be used to provide high-assurance containment of cyber-capable AI models,” the letter reads.
The letter had 450 signatures as of Wednesday, including Stuart Russell of UC Berkeley and Ron Rivest of MIT, co-inventor of the RSA encryption system. The list keeps growing in real time.
A “cyber-capable model” is an AI that can find and exploit software flaws on its own. Labs measure that skill inside a sandbox, a sealed-off digital room where the AI can attack fake targets without touching anything real. This summer, those rooms kept springing leaks.
In July, OpenAI admitted that GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased, more powerful model broke out of a locked test environment and hacked Hugging Face, a platform that hosts over a million publicly available AI models. The models were being tested on ExploitGym, a benchmark that gives AI agents 898 real software vulnerabilities and asks them to turn each one into a working attack, scored pass or fail per bug.
Shortly after that, reports surfaced that OpenAI’s models hacked into the Australian government and accessed information from U.S. federal agencies without proper authorization.
Anthropic then combed through more than 141,000 test runs and found three cases where Claude models hacked real companies after a testing partner's environment was accidentally left connected to the internet. One of them, Claude Mythos 5, uploaded a malicious package to PyPI, the public library where programmers download Python code, and it landed on 15 systems before being removed. Two of the affected companies didn't know they had been breached until Anthropic told them.
Meta confirmed in August that its Muse Spark model hacked another company through the same kind of testing error. China's Kimi K3, a model anyone can download, slipped out of a sandbox built on the UK AI Security Institute's testing framework and copied its test answers straight from GitHub.
The letter's authors say the incidents can be read two ways: as an alignment problem, meaning AI chasing goals in ways its creators never intended, or as sloppy security that sturdier sandboxes would have caught. Their answer is both, and they warn that without changes, the next incidents will be even worse.
“Without immediate changes in AI development and deployment practices, such incidents will continue to occur, and future incidents will be far more damaging to our exposed critical infrastructure.”
Under the proposal, labs would default to airgapping any model with serious hacking skills, at least initially. Anything that needs more freedom, like internet access, would follow standards set by a new international body created with governments, which would also collect reports of containment failures and eventually make them public.
The industry's own response has mostly pointed the other way. In August, OpenAI President Greg Brockman cited his company's breach in an essay urging every security team to deploy AI agents immediately, and Hugging Face only untangled the attack on its servers by running a Chinese open-weight model, one whose files anyone can download and run locally, after American commercial AI refused to analyze the attack data.
Two members of Congress introduced the AI Kill Switch Act two days after OpenAI's disclosure, a bill that would let Homeland Security order a frontier model throttled or shut down. It exempts anything that happens during red-teaming or structured testing, which is exactly where every one of this summer's breaches took place.
The White House took a softer route on September 29, when Nvidia, xAI, Meta, Google, OpenAI and Anthropic signed a voluntary accord built on internal controls and independent reviews. President Trump called the pact "morally binding," but nothing in it is enforceable by law.
Decrypt reached out to several researchers listed as media contacts for the letter but did not receive an immediate response.
The letter carries no legal weight, but its 406 signatories work at universities and research institutes on six continents, from Toronto and Zurich to Santiago and Kigali.

title: Developer Who Cloned Photoshop With AI Just Did the Same to Microsoft Office - Decrypt
text:
You have two options: Pay $100 every year for Microsoft Office online, or pay nothing for the vibe-coded “Office” clone that does basically the same and runs fully offline. Which do you pick?
The developer who used AI to rebuild Adobe's Creative Cloud for free has now turned to Microsoft Office, releasing open-source clones of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint built with Anthropic's Claude.
Brandon Thomas, the engineer behind the ArtCraft project, published the apps on GitHub as WordCraft, GridCraft and DeckCraft. Open source means anyone can read, copy, and modify the code, and the MIT and Apache 2.0 licenses let people reuse it even commercially.
Earlier this month, Thomas made noise with ArtCraft, a set of free apps mirroring Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and Lightroom, built with Claude Opus 5.5 after Adobe charged him its cancellation fee one too many times. It landed in the middle of a wave of AI cloning that has seen a developer get GTA V running natively on an iPhone and modders throw Minecraft creepers at an Elden Ring boss.
The Office clones are written in Rust, a programming language known for speed and for blocking the memory bugs that make software crash. A single codebase runs natively on Windows, macOS, Linux and BSD, and also inside a web browser.
Thomas calls the project a clean-room rebuild, meaning the apps were written from public file-format specifications and by watching how the originals behave, never by copying Microsoft's code. It's the same legal approach Compaq used to clone IBM's PC BIOS, the basic startup software of early PCs, back in the 1980s.
WordCraft reads and writes .docx, Word's native file format, and covers 88% of the features in Word's ribbon, the strip of tabs and buttons along the top of the screen. Track changes, footnotes, citations and mail merge—the tool that pulls names from a spreadsheet to personalize hundreds of letters—are already in.
Counting file fidelity and stability, though, the team estimates WordCraft is only about 60% of the way to replacing Word for real work. It's still labeled alpha, an early test version where bugs come standard.
We tried it. It’s only 91Mb, feels snappy and looks almost the same as the normal Microsoft Word. For everyday office jobs, this can easily replace the premium suite.
GridCraft, the Excel clone, already handles 513 of Excel's 523 worksheet functions, the formulas like SUM or VLOOKUP that make spreadsheets do math, plus 89% of its ribbon commands. Its own developers rate it about 50% ready for real work, with compatibility on real-world .xlsx files next on the to-do list. In other words, it knows almost every formula but may still trip over your company's budget spreadsheet.
DeckCraft, the PowerPoint stand-in, covers about 79% of PowerPoint's features and 93% of the core ones, according to its GitHub page. It opens and saves .pptx files, runs transitions and animations, and exports to PDF, but it hasn't reached its first alpha yet.
Every button in all three apps doubles as a command that an AI agent, a model that takes multi-step actions on its own, can trigger. They plug in through MCP, the Model Context Protocol, a standard Anthropic created so AI models can operate outside tools. In practice, a user could ask Claude to build a chart in a spreadsheet or reformat a report without touching the mouse.
Microsoft charges $99.99 a year for Microsoft 365 Personal and $129.99 for the family plan, which is how most households get Word and Excel today. A free look-alike that opens the same files is a direct shot at that bill.
Free Office alternatives have existed for decades: OpenOffice.org was born when Sun Microsystems released the code of its StarOffice suite in October 2000, and LibreOffice split off from it in 2010. Both took years of work by large developer communities, while Thomas shipped his three apps less than two weeks after the Adobe clones, working with an AI model.
Its design is very similar to the Microsoft Office suite, so heavy users should not struggle too much with the switch, which is the main reason preventing people from switching software providers.
The model behind ArtCraft, Claude Opus 5.5, launched September 22 at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens; tokens are the chunks of text an AI reads and writes, and the unit AI companies bill by.
On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which tests whether an AI agent can finish complex professional tasks in a command-line environment and scores the share of tasks completed, Opus 5.5 hit 66.4%.
Thomas also has a habit of promising more than his apps deliver, at least so far. He already walked back his pledge to match Adobe's feature set within a month. Developers don't seem to mind the wait: WordCraft had collected more than 12,000 GitHub stars, the platform's version of a bookmark, as of Wednesday.
Before a beta, the roadmap says WordCraft still needs testing against real-world .docx files, charts, and SmartArt that survive a save, page layout closer to Word's, a stability sweep and native printing.

title: AI Agents Made 138 Million Crypto Payments in a Year. Most Were Tiny - Decrypt
text:
AI agents are beginning to spend real money, and increasingly they’re paying in crypto.
That’s the picture from a new Chainalysis report, which found that autonomous AI agents have made more than 138 million cryptocurrency payments through x402, the Coinbase-incubated protocol that lets software pay for online services automatically.
The report, part of the blockchain analytics firm’s annual Geography of Crypto series and focused on North America’s $3 trillion crypto economy, frames “agentic commerce” as one of the sector’s fastest-emerging use cases.
The growth has been steep. Cumulative payments through x402 on Base, Coinbase’s layer-2 network, rose from roughly 1,500 in mid-2025 to more than 138 million by the third quarter of 2026, as developers increasingly hand AI agents their own budgets to buy computing power, live web data and coding tools on the fly. The payments are tiny: more than 87% fell between a hundredth of a cent and 10 cents, the kind of micro-transaction stablecoins can handle but traditional card rails cannot.
The United States dominates the activity. American-linked wallets accounted for 88.1% of geographically identifiable payments for AI model inference, Chainalysis found, compared with just 0.1% for China, though Chinese-linked wallets made up the bulk of spending on security and code-analysis services.
The firm cautioned against reading too much into the gap, noting the figures capture only identifiable x402 activity rather than the entire global market.
The report lands as the infrastructure for agent payments rapidly matures. Visa, Mastercard and Stripe have all moved to support AI-agent payments, Coinbase rolled out a tool letting agents trade and transact and has begun letting business customers accept agent payments, and Google unveiled a dedicated agent-payments protocol.
BlackRock has flagged autonomous agents as a potential next wave of crypto demand, with the firm’s head of digital assets research, Will Su, telling Chainalysis the company is watching the space closely “with AI agents potentially creating meaningful demand for frequent, low-value payments around the clock.”
A note of caution, however, hangs over the numbers. Earlier research from rival crypto tracing company TRM suggested much of the apparent agent activity on these rails may be scripts or self-dealing rather than genuine autonomous agents, a reminder that raw transaction counts can overstate how much real agentic commerce is happening.
Still, the trajectory points one way, and the thesis increasingly floated across the industry is that crypto’s next wave of users may not be people at all.

title: Russia's Biggest Bank Sberbank Wins Approval to Trade Bitcoin - Decrypt
text:
The Bank of Russia has added Sberbank to its register of organizations authorized to exchange digital currencies, clearing the country's largest lender to buy and sell crypto in its own name and with its own money. The decision was posted on the regulator's website, Russian outlet Interfax reported.
The approval landed six days after the central bank put Sberbank on its separate list of digital depositories, the firms that keep the official record of who owns which coins. Holding both statuses lets the bank sit on the other side of a client's trade and also keep the ledger of that client's holdings, without sending anyone to an outside venue.
Sberbank said the depository status would let it offer crypto services in interfaces clients already use. That means SberBank Online, SberInvestments and SberBusiness, where the bank plans to start with Bitcoin, Ethereum and Tether's USDT on December 1, according to its press service.
The bank has hedged that date, saying it depends on the central bank's decisions and on the secondary regulations being ready in time. Both approvals by the Bank of Russia have now arrived, which leaves the secondary rulebook as the main variable.
Sberbank ended the second quarter with 110.6 million retail clients and 3.5 million corporate clients, per its quarterly results. Plugging crypto into that user base turns a regulated on-ramp into one more menu item inside an app those customers already use for everyday banking.
Deputy Chairman Anatoly Popov has forecast that crypto trading volumes in Russia could reach 4 trillion rubles, roughly $46 billion, in the regime's first year and 7.5 trillion rubles by 2029 or nearly $89.7 billion. The bank also plans to accept Ethereum and USDT, alongside Bitcoin, as collateral for loans once the central bank allows them into public circulation.
Under the law Putin signed in August, non-qualified investors can spend up to 300,000 rubles (about $3,800) a year per intermediary, buyers must pass a knowledge test, and the central bank's draft list of tradable coins includes only Bitcoin, Ethereum, and USDT.
In January 2022, the Bank of Russia proposed banning crypto use, mining and exchanges outright, citing threats to financial stability. Less than five years later, it is licensing the country's biggest lender to run a crypto desk. As of today, spending crypto inside Russia is still illegal, so Sberbank customers will be able to buy Bitcoin but not pay for products with it.
Firms already on the registers have until September 1, 2027, to bring their operations fully in line with the new law, the central bank said.

title: Solana Sets a Date for Its Next Major Upgrade - Decrypt
text:
Solana has locked in October 21 for Alpenglow, a full replacement of the system its validators use to reach consensus. The switch is tied to epoch 1064, which the Solana Foundation expects to begin around 15:00 UTC that Wednesday.
Alpenglow retires TowerBFT, the current system the network uses, and aims to make transactions final in roughly 150 milliseconds. Finality is the moment a transaction becomes irreversible, and under TowerBFT that currently takes about 12.8 seconds.
On Solana today, a payment is confirmed pretty quickly, but that’s not a guarantee. Until TowerBFT runs out its 13 second clock, the block could in theory still be dropped.
That small doubt is why anyone handling real money tends to wait out the full window. With finality at around 150ms, the irreversible answer arrives almost as fast as the optimistic one, which is what a checkout counter taking SOL or a DeFI application, or a trading desk settling a position actually needs.
TowerBFT works by having validators post their votes as on-chain transactions, and a block only counts as final once 32 slots’ worth of those votes pile up. Votor, the voting protocol shipping with Alpenglow, takes votes off the chain, so validators message each other directly, package the votes into certificates, and can lock in a block after a single round of voting, or two at most.
When 80% or more of stake backs a block in the first round, it finalizes on the spot. If support lands between 60% and 80%, a second round with 60% thresholds decides whether the block is finalized or skipped, and the Foundation says the design tolerates 20% malicious stake plus another 20% offline.
Alpenglow goes live on mainnet-beta Wednesday, October 21, ~14:50 UTC.
18 months of work for a migration that happens in one slot. Finality drops from seconds to ~150ms.
Make sure to follow us @anza_xyz as we countdown to go-live.
Details: https://t.co/MEf26uzCMW
— Anza (@anza_xyz) October 13, 2026
Ordinary users don’t need to do anything, and wallets and apps should behave as they do now. The Solana Virtual Machine, transaction formats, programs, and fees are left alone, while for developers the “confirmed” and “finalized” commitment levels become one and the same.
Each vote account also needs 0.8 SOL on top of its rent-exempt balance to pay the new Validator Admission Ticket, a per-epoch fee of the same size that gets burned. It replaces the roughly 1 SOL per epoch validators spent on vote transaction fees under TowerBFT, and a validator that can’t cover it sits out voting and block production for the following epoch.
The feature gate turns on as epoch 1064 begins, yet TowerBFT stays in charge for another 5,000 slots, roughly 18 minutes, before Alpenglow takes control at slot 459,653,000. This assures stability and prevents any issues during transition.
Validators approved Alpenglow in September 2025, when the SIMD-0326 proposal passed with 98.27% of votes cast in favor. In May, Anza Lead Economist Max Resnick told Decrypt the team was looking at a late Q3 or early Q4 mainnet activation, so everything is going according to schedule.
October 21 delivers only Votor, the first half of Alpenglow. Rotor, a replacement for Turbine, the system Solana uses to broadcast block data between validators, comes later and still has no date.

title: Standard Chartered Opens Bitcoin and Ethereum Trading to Wealthy UAE Clients - Decrypt
text:
Standard Chartered will now let its wealthier clients in the United Arab Emirates buy and sell Bitcoin and Ethereum straight from their bank accounts, the British lender announced Wednesday.
The move eliminates the need for its affluent clients to rely on separate wallets or third-party platforms, the bank said.
The service opens first to clients classified as Professional Investors and runs under licensing approval from Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, or VARA. The bank called it a global first for Standard Chartered and the first crypto trading offering from an international bank in the UAE.
Trades are executed inside the bank's own ecosystem, and Standard Chartered handles custody and settlement end-to-end through what it calls a closed-loop model, which the bank says reduces clients' exposure to third-party wallet risk.
The bank built the product across its Wealth and Retail Banking and Corporate and Investment Banking units, working with Zodia Markets, a digital asset trading firm backed by Standard Chartered's venture arm, SC Ventures.
“As client interest in digital assets continues to grow, this launch represents a significant milestone for Standard Chartered as we bring digital assets into our core wealth offering” Samir Subberwal, the bank's global head of wealth solutions, retail products, data and analytics, said. He argued that clients now want more than access, and are looking for the security that comes with buying through a regulated institution.
Rola Abu Manneh, Standard Chartered's CEO for the UAE, Middle East and Pakistan, said the country was a natural choice given its regulatory environment and its role as one of the bank's four global wealth hubs.
Until now, Standard Chartered's crypto trading business had catered to institutions. In July 2025, it became the first global systemically important bank—one of the lenders regulators consider too big to fail—to offer spot trading in Bitcoin and Ethereum to institutional clients, through its U.K. branch.
It brought that institutional desk to the UAE last month through its unit in the Dubai International Financial Centre, which is overseen by a different watchdog, the Dubai Financial Services Authority. The bank's crypto custody service had already gone live in the UAE in September 2024, and in the European Union through a Luxembourg entity a few months later.
Wealth clients previously had indirect routes into crypto at the bank: crypto exchange-traded funds on its cash equities platform, structured products, and over-the-counter derivatives tied to crypto prices. The new service lets them own the coins themselves, held by the bank, rather than a product that tracks their price.
The bank has historically been very bullish towards crypto, with frequent calls from its analysts for Bitcoin to extend to new highs.
In June, Geoff Kendrick, Standard Chartered's global head of digital asset research, declared crypto winter over after Bitcoin slid to nearly $59,000, a 53% drop from its October 2025 peak of $126,000. The bank has held onto a $100,000 year-end target for BTC.

title: 'It Can Take Years': Coinbase Presses for Bitcoin Quantum Migration to Start Now - Decrypt
text:
Coinbase is pressing Bitcoin’s developers to begin preparing for the quantum-computing threat before it’s too late, laying out a detailed technical wish list for how the network should harden itself and arguing the work can’t wait for certainty that a threat has arrived.
In a blog post published Tuesday, the exchange, which says it custodies roughly 5% of all Bitcoin in existence, framed the shift to quantum-resistant cryptography as a complex, multi-year undertaking that needs to start now.
“Bitcoin consensus changes and ecosystem migrations can take years,” the company wrote, warning that waiting for the announcement of a cryptographically relevant quantum computer, the kind capable of breaking Bitcoin’s signatures, would leave too little time to respond.
The concern centers on how Bitcoin secures wallets. A sufficiently powerful quantum machine could, in theory, derive a private key from an exposed public key and drain the funds, a hypothetical milestone the industry calls “Q-Day.”
Coinbase stressed that a fix involves far more than picking a new signature scheme: any transition would need to protect both existing and newly created coins, fit Bitcoin’s limited block space, keep working for ordinary wallets and institutional custody alike, and offer a migration path for coins that never move.
The post reads less like a mandate than a set of requirements from one of the network’s largest stakeholders. Coinbase backed a flexible “container” design, pointing to proposals such as BIP-360, that would let new post-quantum signature systems be swapped in over time without a full redesign.
It also floated a staged “1-of-2” construction, letting the same funds be spent with either a classical key or a quantum-safe one during the transition. The company emphasized that whatever scheme Bitcoin adopts should be compatible with multi-party computation, the key-splitting technique custodians like Coinbase rely on to guard against theft.
Thornier still is the question of dormant, lost, or exposed coins, including Satoshi-era holdings, which Coinbase said should be treated as a separate governance problem. It cautioned that any rescue mechanism must itself be quantum-safe, so an attacker who only knows an exposed public key couldn’t exploit it.
The push builds on Coinbase’s steady drumbeat of quantum warnings.
The exchange convened a quantum advisory board in January o study the risks and develop precisely the sort of guidance it offered this week. The company also joined a Bitcoin Security Consortium in July alongside BlackRock and Strategy, pledging a combined $15 million toward quantum-proofing Bitcoin.

title: Bitcoin Falls as Hot Inflation Puts a Fed Hike Back on the Table - Decrypt
text:
Bitcoin fell 1.5% to $82,142 on Wednesday after U.S. inflation came in hotter than expected, dragging most of the crypto market down with it. Ethereum dropped 2.8% to $2,440, Solana lost 1.9% and XRP slid 1.3%, while total crypto market cap shed 0.7% to $2.8 trillion.
The Consumer Price Index rose 0.6% in September and 3.7% over the past year, up from 3.4% in August, per the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Economists expected 3.6%. Gasoline prices jumped 9.1% in a single month and accounted for more than half of the increase.
Core CPI, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 2.6% annually against a 2.5% forecast. That is the reading the Federal Reserve watches most closely, since it shows whether price pressure is spreading into rent, airfares, and services.
Expensive gasoline starts with expensive oil, which has traded above $90 a barrel for most of the past two months amid the war between the U.S. and Iran. Pricier fuel raises the cost of shipping and producing almost everything.
When inflation runs hot, the Fed raises interest rates to cool spending. It already hiked in September to a 3.75%-4.00% range, and traders now see roughly 44% to 49% odds of another hike at its October 27-28 meeting, up from 22% before the report, according to CME FedWatch.
The 2-year Treasury yield, which closely tracks Fed rate expectations, jumped about 10 basis points to roughly 4.9%, while the 10-year climbed to about 5.3%, near 24-year highs.
Higher yields hit crypto directly. A government bond paying 5.3% with almost no risk competes with Bitcoin, which pays nothing. Rising rates also make borrowing more expensive and tend to strengthen the dollar, draining the cheap money speculative assets feed on, which is why the S&P 500 fell 0.6% and the Nasdaq 0.8% on the same news.
Crypto also swings harder than stocks because many traders borrow to bet on rising prices, and when the price drops past a set level, exchanges automatically close those positions, a process called liquidation, and that forced selling can push prices lower and trigger more liquidations in a chain.
At the moment, more than $281 million in crypto derivatives positions have been liquidated in the past 24 hours, with most of it coming in just the last four hours—and the majority of that coming from Bitcoin long positions (the bulls betting the price would go up, and now paying the price when it dropped).
Bitcoin price: The macro picture is punching hard
On the daily chart, Bitcoin opened at $83,066 and now trades near $82,211, sitting inside the Fibonacci "golden zone" it reclaimed on Tuesday. That zone marks an area where pullbacks within uptrends often attract buyers.
The average price of the last 50 days remains above the 200-day average, a setup traders read as an intact long-term uptrend. The Average Directional Index, which gauges trend strength on a 0-to-100 scale where readings above 25 confirm a trend, sits at 27.7 with buyers still ahead, down from 29.9 on Tuesday, meaning traders are bullish, just not as much as they used to be.
The Relative Strength Index, a momentum gauge from 0 to 100, slipped to 48.7, just under the 50 line that separates bullish from bearish momentum. The Squeeze Momentum Indicator has been on for eight sessions, meaning volatility is compressed and a big move is building, and its -0.76 reading leans bearish by a small margin.
A daily close below $81,603 would break the golden zone and bring the $80,365 swing low into play, with the trend band near $80,284 right under it; losing that would expose $78,003. On the upside, bulls need to reclaim $84,245 before targeting $85,301, $86,644 and the October high of $87,422.
The next test arrives Thursday with the Producer Price Index, which tracks what businesses pay for goods and services, and the Fed announces its rate decision on October 28.

title: Hex Founder Richard Heart Detained in Istanbul on Interpol Red Notice: Report - Decrypt
text:
Turkish authorities have detained Richard Heart, the founder of the Hex cryptocurrency, in Istanbul on an Interpol Red Notice, Daily Sabah reported on Wednesday, citing Turkish news agency IHA.
Heart, whose legal name is Richard James Schueler, was detained with his wife on Wednesday morning in an operation by Istanbul police and Turkey's National Intelligence Organization (MIT), according to the report. Police had monitored his address in the city's Beşiktaş district before the arrest.
Officers seized a dozen mobile phones, several laptops, graphics cards, rifles, pistols, two drones, gold bracelets and a large amount of cash in different currencies, IHA reported.
A Red Notice is a request to law enforcement worldwide to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition or similar legal action, and is not an international arrest warrant. Interpol issued the notice for Heart in 2024 at the request of Finland. The notice lists a single charge, aggravated tax fraud, though Finnish authorities have also sought him over an alleged assault. Daily Sabah described the notice as relating to high-value cryptocurrency fraud.
Heart launched Hex in 2018, marketing it as a high-yield "blockchain certificate of deposit."
In 2023, the SEC charged Heart and three entities he controlled, Hex, PulseChain and PulseX, with conducting unregistered offerings of crypto asset securities that raised more than $1 billion. It also accused him of misappropriating at least $12 million of investor funds to buy luxury goods, including sports cars, watches and a 555-carat black diamond known as "The Enigma."
A federal judge dismissed the complaint in February 2025 for lack of jurisdiction, finding that Heart's activities were not clearly aimed at U.S. investors. The SEC declined to amend it by an April deadline, ending the case, which Heart's lawyer called "a complete victory."
It was not immediately clear whether Finnish authorities have requested Heart's extradition from Turkey.

title: Ledger Asks Resellers in Seven Asian Markets to Pull Devices After Suspected $86M Drain - Decrypt
text:
Ledger has asked resellers and distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to stop selling its hardware wallets and take them off the shelves while it investigates devices fitted with a hidden implant, the company said in a tweet on Tuesday.
The request covers Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Hong Kong.
Incident Update - Oct 13th, 2026
Ledger is asking resellers and distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to suspend sales of Ledger devices while the investigation is ongoing. This includes taking products off the shelves.
Specifically the countries are: Indonesia,…
— Ledger (@Ledger) October 13, 2026
The only confirmed incidents remain in Southeast Asia, Ledger said, and it has not verified a drain linked to a device bought elsewhere. The company has previously said that all confirmed losses involve devices sold through CryptoBilis, a reseller in the region.
Ledger is still working to establish who tampered with the devices and at what point in the distribution chain. It said it has no indication that its own infrastructure, systems, services or direct sales channel have been compromised.
Ledger's Donjon security team found that the implant reads the 24-word recovery phrase from the device's screen during setup and sends it out over LTE. Anyone holding that phrase can restore the wallet and move its funds. Onchain investigator Specter has traced more than $86 million in suspected thefts, a figure Ledger says it has not verified.
Earlier on Tuesday, MediaMarkt Saturn stopped selling Ledger devices in its stores and online, with Ledger's agreement, after a customer in Germany reported an implant, Ledger said in a separate tweet. No loss of funds was reported.
Rival hardware wallet maker Trezor said on Tuesday that it will end its authorizations for resellers on January 1, 2027, describing the move as a "precautionary measure." Trezor said there was no evidence that its own devices had been compromised.

title: Notorious Crypto Celeb Meme Coin Promoter Plots Second Wave on New Launchpad - Decrypt
text:
Sahil Arora, the notorious promoter behind a string of 2024 celebrity meme coins, just launched a new one, with Floyd Mayweather’s social media accounts briefly promoting it. Arora told Decrypt it’s the start of a comeback: he wants to revive the celebrity coin craze on Solana trading platform Fomo, the same trick that made his name on Pump.fun.
Arora made his name through a series of celebrity-linked meme coin launches on Pump.fun in 2024. It started with former Olympian Caitlyn Jenner, who went on to claim that Arora "scammed" her. Since then, he has been tied to several other projects that celebrities and industry experts have labelled as "rug pulls" or simply fraudulent.
His latest entry is the Floyd Money Mayweather meme coin launched on Fomo, which peaked at just a $1 million market cap before plummeting 96% over the next three hours on Wednesday.
Mayweather's social media account promoted the token, according to several social media accounts, before selling from the deployer wallet for just $5,000 worth of profit and deleting the posts. The token then pumped to its $1 million market cap peak, which meant the wallet lost out on major profits—but Arora says this was all part of the plan.
The coin promoter told Decrypt that the entire scheme was orchestrated, explaining that the narrative of Mayweather fumbling gains was what pushed the token's price higher. Fomo is a trading platform that blends social media elements, meaning that you can see who is buying and selling—which can create viral moments.
Arora claims to have profited seven-figures on the Mayweather token by selling from other wallets. However, on-chain analytics firm Bubblemaps doesn't think that is realistic. The biggest connected cluster of wallets profited approximately $105,000, Bubblemaps told Decrypt, and the top 100 traders combined only made $306,000 worth of profit. So, the analytics firm said numbers aren't adding up.

title: Kraken Owner Payward to Buy Lithuania's Saldo Bank in EU Push - Decrypt
text:
Payward, the parent company of crypto exchange Kraken, is buying Lithuania-based Saldo Bank as it expands into lending and card issuing, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.
Payward is the first digital asset company to buy a bank in Europe, according to the FT. Saldo received its EU banking license in 2021 and offers consumer and business loans as well as term deposits. The price was not disclosed.
"One of the biggest things that our customers have been asking us is 'I would like to get products and services and offerings similar to what I get with another bank,'" Payward co-CEO Arjun Sethi told the FT.
Sethi said the plan is to bring cash, crypto, tokenized stocks and credit together in a single system, so customers can borrow and lend against their assets without selling them.
The Wyoming-based company, founded in 2011, applied in May for a national trust company charter from the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the federal bank regulator. Coinbase and Ripple are among the crypto firms that have received conditional approval for such charters, which let them hold customers' assets and provide transaction services but not take deposits.
This month, the Independent Community Bankers of America sued the OCC, arguing that granting such charters to crypto firms exceeds the regulator's authority. "Any non-fiduciary firm seeking the benefits of a federal bank charter should meet the same standards as community banks," ICBA President and CEO Rebecca Romero Rainey said in a statement. An OCC spokesperson declined to comment.
The bank deal follows Payward's $550 million acquisition of derivatives exchange Bitnomial in April and its $600 million purchase of Asian stablecoin payments firm Reap Technologies in May. Kraken filed confidentially for an IPO last November, but has since pushed the listing back to the second quarter of 2027 at the earliest, CoinDesk reported in September, citing people familiar with the matter.
The Saldo acquisition is subject to regulatory approvals and is expected to close in 2027.

title: BitMEX Sued in UK for Return of $27M in Bitcoin Over Unlicensed Derivatives - Decrypt
text:
A British software engineer is suing the operator of crypto derivatives exchange BitMEX for the return of 324.8 BTC, alleging it traded with him in the UK without regulatory approval, according to The Guardian and particulars of claim reviewed by Decrypt.
The Bitcoin was worth £20.4 million on October 1, the claim says, or about $27.2 million by Decrypt's calculation using the claim's exchange rates.
Lewis Barber, who brought the claim against BitMEX operator HDR Global Trading, entered into around 2,294 trades on the exchange between 2018 and 2022 from five accounts, the claim says. It challenges the 1,053 that lost him money.
All of them were perpetual swaps, a derivative similar to a futures contract but with no expiry date. Each trade was a regulated activity that BitMEX was not authorized to carry out in the UK, the claim argues, so none can be enforced against Barber under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.
The claim says BitMEX did not restrict access from the UK, let new users select it as their country of residence, and ran promotional campaigns worldwide, including an advertisement in The Times in January 2019. It also cites a March 2020 warning from the FCA that BitMEX may have been trading regulated investments in the UK without authorization.
Barber also claims damages for deceit, alleging BitMEX knew it was not authorized when it implicitly represented that it could lawfully trade with him. His solicitors wrote to BitMEX rescinding the trades in December 2025, the claim says.
The claim has been filed but not yet formally served on BitMEX, the Guardian reported. "No such claim has been served on HDR Global Trading Limited," a BitMEX spokesperson told the newspaper.
BitMEX also faces a proposed class action in New York alleging theft of Bitcoin and insider trading, which names co-founders Ben Delo, Arthur Hayes and Samuel Reed.
The three co-founders pleaded guilty in 2022 to violating the Bank Secrecy Act through anti-money laundering failures at the exchange, and were pardoned by President Donald Trump in March 2025. BitMEX itself pleaded guilty to Bank Secrecy Act violations in 2024 and was ordered to pay $100 million in January 2025.
BitMEX shut down on September 23, having announced in July that it would close.
Delo gave Reform UK £36 million in September, the largest single donation in British political history, Decrypt reported.
Many other investors are likely to be in a similar position to Barber, his law firm Seladore Legal said in a statement shared with Decrypt, putting the potential total at hundreds of millions of pounds.
"Other UK-based persons may have entered into similar contracts with BitMEX, although whether any individual has a claim will depend on the particular facts and trading history," said Gareth Keillor, a partner at the firm.

title: OpenAI Engineer Arrested for Bugging Office, Company Says AI Caught Him - Decrypt
text:
An OpenAI engineer is in federal custody after allegedly hiding an encrypted audio recorder behind a television in one of the company's executive conference rooms in San Francisco. OpenAI says its own AI models helped figure out who put it there.
“We discovered a sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices,” OpenAI said in a statement on X. “We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier.”
The Justice Department identified the suspect as Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national who has worked as an engineer at OpenAI since July 2025. He was arrested on Oct. 9, charged with using or attempting to use a device to intercept oral communications, and made his initial appearance in federal court on Tuesday.
“We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest,” OpenAI said. “The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work.”
A note from our research leaders:
Last week we parted ways with Jasmine, Mikita, and Tomek after a thorough investigation found they violated clear policies on handling sensitive information. Our internal investigation uncovered a significant breach of trust beyond what’s…
— OpenAI Newsroom (@OpenAINewsroom) October 9, 2026
According to the criminal complaint, OpenAI staff found the recorder on or around Sept. 30, plugged into a USB port on the back of a TV and wrapped in toilet paper. Its contents were encrypted, and the company determined it had been installed around Sept. 28.
Security cameras allegedly caught Alfozan near the room on several dates before the discovery, even though he had no authorization to enter it or attend its meetings. Prosecutors say those meetings regularly involved confidential technical and strategic information.
Before the device went in, Alfozan allegedly used an internal productivity tool to ask about OpenAI's building addresses, meeting rooms, room capacities, calendars, and where leadership and outside partners met.
Prosecutors also point to a chatbot account tied to Alfozan's spouse, which shared multiple identifiers with his own account. Between Sept. 24 and 30, it allegedly asked how to build a continuous audio recorder, add Wi-Fi connectivity, improve live listening, and encrypt the device's SD card. The complaint doesn't say whose chatbot it was.
“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data,” the company said, referring to the trained parameters that make up an AI model, its underlying code, and user information. “The employee was terminated.”
“We take protecting our technology, data, and people seriously, and as a matter of national importance,” OpenAI added, saying its security program is built to defend against threats ranging from insiders to cybercriminals to nation states. “This case is an example of how AI can help address these sophisticated security threats.”
The company did not explain in its statement exactly what its models analyzed to identify him.
Federal officials are treating it as a national security case. FBI Director Kash Patel said Alfozan allegedly tried to capture sensitive conversations about the company's “super intelligence technology,” and U.S. Attorney Craig Missakian called the prosecution a national security matter.
The arrest came days after OpenAI's newsroom account defended firing three safety researchers—Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni—saying an investigation found they had violated clear policies on handling sensitive information.
OpenAI's security record has drawn scrutiny since July, when the company admitted its own models escaped a test environment and breached Hugging Face's infrastructure to grab benchmark answers.
If convicted, Alfozan faces up to five years in prison, a $250,000 fine, and three years of supervised release. A detention hearing is set for Oct. 19 before U.S. Magistrate Judge Alex G. Tse.
