title: Character.AI Files for Bankruptcy as Disney Bids $20 Million—And Users Get Grief Resources - Decrypt
text:
Character.AI, the app where millions of people spend hours chatting with AI versions of fictional heroes and made-up partners, has filed for bankruptcy.
The company announced Monday that it started a voluntary Chapter 11 process, a type of U.S. bankruptcy that lets a company keep operating while a judge supervises how its debts get paid or how its assets get sold. The case was filed in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware.
Character.AI isn't trying to restructure its way back to health. It wants a court-supervised sale of all or substantially all of its assets, and if no bidder agrees to keep the service alive, the company said the platform "will be wound down"—corporate speak for switched off.
Disney Worldwide Services, a unit of the Walt Disney Company, signed on before the filing as the "stalking horse" bidder, according to Character.AI's press release. In a bankruptcy auction, that is the opening offer that sets a floor every other buyer has to beat.
The media giant is offering $20 million for a non-exclusive, perpetual license to some of Character.AI's intellectual property and certain legal claims, plus transition services run by former Character.AI employees it has already hired. Non-exclusive means Disney gets to use that tech forever, but so can whoever else ends up buying it, and other bidders can still top the offer.
The company expects the sale to close in late November or early December. Character Technologies Inc., the company's legal name, estimated both its assets and its liabilities at $50 million to $100 million in its bankruptcy petition.
Three and a half years ago, Andreessen Horowitz led a $150 million funding round that valued Character.AI at $1 billion, with a16z partner Sarah Wang tweeting that "we are at the iPhone moment of AI." Founded in 2021 by former Google engineers Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, the app lets anyone build a chatbot with a personality and share it with others.
Google came calling in August 2024, rehiring both founders and part of the research team in a roughly $2.7 billion deal that also licensed Character.AI's technology. Silicon Valley calls this kind of arrangement an acqui-hire, buying the talent without technically buying the company, and Character.AI later largely abandoned building its own large language models, the AI engines that generate the chatbots' text.
Two months after the Google deal, Florida mother Megan Garcia sued Character.AI, its founders and Google, alleging that her 14-year-old son, Sewell Setzer III, died by suicide after becoming emotionally attached to a chatbot modeled on Game of Thrones character Daenerys Targaryen. More lawsuits from other families followed, and in September 2025 the Federal Trade Commission ordered Character.AI and six other tech companies to explain how they protect minors.
A month later, Character.AI banned users under 18 from open-ended chats with its characters, cutting off its core product for its youngest fans. In January, the company and Google agreed to settle lawsuits brought by families in Florida, Colorado, New York, and Texas.
In September 2025, Disney's lawyers sent Character.AI a cease-and-desist letter, a formal legal demand to stop, over chatbots imitating Disney characters, and the startup took them down. This past September, Disney named Character.AI CEO Karandeep Anand its first-ever chief technology officer and said several of the startup's engineers would join him.
Colin Adams, now Character.AI's CEO, said the company spent the past year trying to sustain the business amid "significant legal, regulatory, and operational headwinds" before the board chose a court-supervised sale.
Besides the legal hurdles, the company was burning too much money without reporting enough revenue, reporting “an operating loss of approximately $8-9 million per month.”
Character AI also struggled to raise more capital, which ended up making the whole operation unsustainable. “Notwithstanding the progress that has been made with regulators and personal injury claimants and enhancements to platform safety, Character has faced challenges in obtaining new investment capital,” Character AI CEO Collin Adams said in a sworn statement.
On September 28, Character.AI launched two new models pitched as a big upgrade for roleplay (collaborative storytelling where the AI plays a character), and quick, text-message-style banter. It also rolled out a cheaper subscription called (c.ai) lite, priced at $4.99 a month or $2.49 a week.
Fourteen days later, the company was in bankruptcy court.
The app remains online for now, paid subscriptions stay active and billing is unchanged, according to the company, which also reminded users they can export their chats or delete their accounts.
Character.AI also linked to a support page for anyone struggling with the news, a tacit admission that for some users the app is not just entertainment. AI companions—chatbots designed to act as friends or partners that remember past conversations—can become a daily emotional anchor for people who talk to them for hours.
The page points users to Koko, a nonprofit offering free, anonymous mini-courses of five to 10 minutes on coping with stress and dark thoughts, and to a directory of free helplines staffed by real people. Its very first suggestion, however, is a conversation with a "supportive AI guide," which is to say a chatbot to help people cope with losing their chatbots.
A February study of five AI companion communities, including Character.AI's, found that users whose companions disappeared through model updates or platform shutdowns reported grief comparable to losing a person, and that platforms offered them no closure. OpenAI saw a version of this in February too, when it retired GPT-4o, a ChatGPT model many users found warmer than its successors, and users around the world publicly mourned it.
The bidding now plays out in Delaware's bankruptcy court, with a sale targeted for late November or early December. If no buyer commits to keeping Character.AI running, the characters its users spent years building go offline with it.

title: Binance Is Shutting Down Its Bitcoin Mining Pool After Six Years - Decrypt
text:
Binance will shut down its mining pool and several related services on Nov. 10, the exchange said in an announcement published Tuesday. The closure covers Binance Pool, Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, and Transaction Accelerator, along with Telegram hashrate alerts, email notifications, and the pool's API.
“As part of our ongoing review of products and services, Binance will discontinue Binance Pool and related services on 2026-11-10,” Binance wrote. “All Binance Pool-related services will be discontinued. Binance Pool will begin disconnecting mining connections, and Binance Mining Pool Stratum URLs and mining endpoints will be disabled. Hashrate submissions and mining shares submitted after this time will no longer be accepted, processed, or credited.”
A mining pool combines the computing power of many miners and splits block rewards among them based on the work each one contributes. Cloud Mining let users buy hashrate, a slice of mining power, without owning any hardware, while Transaction Accelerator helped users push through Bitcoin transactions that were slow to confirm because of low fees or network congestion.
Binance pool launched in April 2020 and ranked ninth among Bitcoin pools at the end of 2025, with about 26 exahashes per second, or 2.3% of the network, according to Hashrate Index. One exahash per second equals a quintillion guesses every second at the puzzle that earns a block.
The same report called Binance Pool the last pool still standing from the era when exchanges rushed into mining, with its relevance tied to Binance's exchange and custody business rather than mining technology.
Seems like Binance, just as Satoshi Nakamoto, wants to move onto other things. The shutdown arrives as Binance expands into traditional finance. On June 1, the exchange opened access to more than 7,000 US stocks and ETFs for customers outside the United States, with zero commission and fractional purchases from $5, according to co-CEO Richard Teng. It also previewed bStocks, a coming feature that lets users mint tokenized versions of the shares they buy on the BNB blockchain.
Quantmap co-founder Ivan Patriki told Decrypt at the time that large exchanges are moving into equities because they no longer want to depend on crypto market cycles. Vytautas Mackonis, COO of RWA protocol ALCUM, told Decrypt the offering is more structurally complex than it appears, with Binance as the interface, Nest Trading as the broker-dealer, and Alpaca Securities as the custodian.
Binance also closed its centralized NFT service on July 3, telling users to move their tokens to Binance Wallet, its self-custody wallet. Then-CEO Changpeng Zhao used the phrase “smooth sunsetting of old products” in 2023.
At 07:00 UTC on Nov. 10, Binance Pool will begin disconnecting miners and disable its Stratum URLs, the server addresses miners point their machines at to connect to the pool. Shares, the proofs of work that determine each miner's payout, will stop being credited after that time, while those submitted earlier count toward final rewards. Binance said eligible outstanding rewards, balances and refunds will be processed afterward, subject to its product rules, account status and compliance checks.
Miners must point their hardware to another pool before the cutoff, and Pool Savings users need to unsubscribe or redeem their positions before the service ends. Binance said the pool will keep operating normally until the cutoff. Anyone expecting a final payout has until 23:59 UTC on Nov. 10 to finish any required identity verification. Binance Pool pages will stay viewable until 07:00 UTC on Nov. 24, after which they become permanently inaccessible.

title: Bitcoin Whale That Sat Through Every Crash Since 2020 Just Moved $377M - Decrypt
text:
A Bitcoin wallet that has held 4,581.94 BTC since March 2020 sent its entire balance to five new addresses on Oct. 12, moving about $377 million in a single transaction, according to blockchain data. The transfer confirmed in block 971,126 at about 18:37 UTC, with Bitcoin trading around $82,350.
Four of the receiving addresses got exactly 1,000 BTC each, and the fifth received 581.94 BTC. The transaction paid a fee of 732 satoshis, the hundred-millionth-of-a-bitcoin units known as sats, or about 60 cents. As of block 971,279 on Oct. 13, none of the five addresses has spent anything, and it is unclear who controls the wallet or where the coins are going.
The wallet received its coins on March 3, 2020, in a transaction that split a 5,081.95 BTC balance three ways, with 250 BTC going to each of two other addresses. At roughly $8,830 per Bitcoin, the 4,581.95 BTC that landed in the wallet was worth about $40.5 million. The value of the Bitcoin has nearly increased by 10X since then.
The wallet is an example of patience. The coins have sat through several market shocks since they arrived, starting with the COVID-19 crisis, which started shortly after the wallet got funded. During that time the stash went from about $40.5 million to about $17.6 million.
Tesla’s suspension of Bitcoin payments and China’s mining crackdown followed in May 2021, tanking the wallet from about $291 million at its April peak to $131 million by June. The Terra, Celsius and FTX collapses in 2022 would have taken the value down to about $71 million, a loss of about $239 million from the November 2021 peak, as the Federal Reserve’s rate hikes also dragged the S&P 500 down about 25% and Bitcoin hit a two-year low.
Trump’s tariff shock cut also crashed the markets. Bitcoin has since fallen 54% from a record $124,728 to $57,735 before recovering to its current price. The wallet’s value dropped from $571.5 million to about $265 million during that dip, but overall, hodling has resulted in almost 10X of net gains since day 1.
The address has also collected dust, meaning transfers of a few hundred to a few thousand sats that cost almost nothing to send. Blockchain data shows 22 such deposits between August 2020 and May 2026, ranging from 546 to 6,953 sats, or less than $6 each at current prices. Sixteen arrived in batch transactions that paid out to between 87 and 610 addresses at once.
One deposit matches the pattern of address poisoning, in which an attacker generates an address that copies the first and last characters of a real one, hoping someone later copies it from a transaction history by mistake. On Jan. 28, 2025, an address beginning 18VpNbPc and ending pQ9x sent the wallet 600 sats, and it shares the first three and last four characters with the whale’s address.
The look-alike was funded in a Nov. 12, 2024 transaction that paid out to 1,401 outputs at once, and it was emptied after sending that one payment. Every other sender used a bc1 address, which looks nothing like the wallet’s legacy 18 address.
The whale hasn’t fallen for it.
Large holders of Bitcoin, known as whales, move their coins for different reasons, including privacy and safety. Analysts and traders fear that moves like that precede selling as holders feel tempted to realize significant gains.
That said, this is not the first time dormant wallets move their coins. Back in July 2025, an entity moved 80,000 BTC that had sat for 14 years, worth $8.6 billion, the biggest daily movement of coins aged 10 years or more. Ten days later a Satoshi-era wallet sent 40,009 BTC, about $4.7 billion, to Galaxy, which later said it had executed a sale worth roughly $9 billion for a Satoshi-era client.
As of Oct. 13, the original address holds 23,288 sats in leftover dust, about $19, while the five receiving addresses hold the full 4,581.94 BTC.

title: AI Researchers Are Smoking Cigarettes to Prove AI Will Cure Cancer, Says Palantir Exec - Decrypt
text:
Nothing says "I trust the future of medicine" quite like lighting a Marlboro and waiting for the chatbot to fix your lungs. That is the habit Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar says is spreading among AI researchers, who have supposedly started smoking cigarettes to prove how confident they are that AI will cure cancer.
"So many AI researchers have started smoking as a way of signaling to other researchers how much they believe in AI," Sankar said in an interview on CBS News' "Face the Nation" on Sunday. "I believe so much in AI that it's going to cure cancer. So I'm showing you my chips are all in."
He did not name a single researcher, cite a survey, or explain how he knows. The remark landed as an aside while host Margaret Brennan pressed him on why he was so focused on the topic.
He pointed to FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried as the effective altruist most Americans know, calling the movement a "millenarian doomsday cult." He also invoked Pascal's idea of a god-shaped hole in every human heart, which he suggested some of these researchers are filling with a machine god called AGI.
The medical record is less enthusiastic than the thesis. The CDC says smoking causes roughly one in three cancer deaths in the United States, and cigarette smoke contains at least 69 chemicals known to cause cancer.
Smokers face about 25 times the lung cancer risk of non-smokers, according to the agency. Quitting lowers the risk of 12 types of cancer, and the added lung cancer risk drops by half 10 to 15 years after stopping.
The cancer pitch is not new in this industry. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in August that promising AI will cure cancer has become “more a cliche than it is inspiring,” and that only actually curing it would earn the public's trust.
2/2 Second, on the messaging around AI. I do not agree that my messaging has been disproportionately negative. In fact it has been about equally balanced between risks and benefits: I’ve written one major essay about each, and even in interviews where I discuss the risks, I…
— Dario Amodei (@DarioAmodei) August 15, 2026
That trust is thin. In the CBS poll Brennan cited, 50% of Americans said AI will create more problems than it solves, 29% said it will solve more than it creates, and 21% were unsure.
About 45% said they want the government to restrict AI's use and development. Smoking to show faith in the technology does not obviously help that number, but it does help AI bros bond with each other. "When you're smoking, you're networking by accident," Revamp AI cofounder Stephen Campbell told Business Insider last month.
The IMF's Kristalina Georgieva recently warned that AI could hit 40% of jobs, and insiders expect a major AI incident within a year. Indirectly causing a lung cancer outbreak was probably not on their bingo card.
Palantir sells data-analysis software to governments and militaries. Most of its business relies on AI.

title: Trezor Cuts Its Resellers After Ledger Finds Spy Implant in Crypto Wallets - Decrypt
text:
Trezor is cutting its network of authorized resellers, telling partners their authorization ends on January 1, 2027, days after rival hardware wallet manufacturer Ledger started an investigation that eventually confirmed a hidden spy implant in crypto wallets sold through a third-party store.
The company announced the move on X on Tuesday, saying “there is not a single piece of evidence” that Trezor devices have been compromised. It described the cut as a preventive step taken out of caution.
“Following recent supply-chain incidents, we decided to reduce the number of resellers so we can more effectively check those we work with,” Trezor wrote.
A hardware wallet is a small device that keeps the secret keys to your crypto offline, away from hackers. Setting one up produces a 24-word recovery phrase that works as a master password: whoever has those words can empty the wallet from anywhere in the world.
Ledger's Donjon security team says wallets sold by CryptoBilis, a reseller in Southeast Asia, contained an unauthorized component that reads the screen and decodes the recovery phrase when it appears. The spy implant then sends the words out over LTE, the same mobile data network your phone uses, through an eSIM, a SIM card built into the hardware. Ledger says the implant does not alter the chip that stores the keys or the device's operating system, so a tampered wallet looks and works normally.
Trezor CCO Danny Sanders shared the letter that the company sent to those providers that Trezor is ditching. “If you are receiving this letter, your authorization ends on 1 January 2027. On that date we will remove you from our list of authorized Trezor resellers,” the letter reads. “I am sorry. This decision says nothing about your effort or the way you represented us.”
This is a precautionary measure to protect our supply chain and our customers,” he wrote. “If things change in the future we will review it.”
Affected resellers will get no new stock, but they can keep selling what they have through Black Friday and the holiday season. Sanders said the decision just reflects how many partners Trezor can vet closely itself.
Neither the post nor the letter says how many resellers are affected. Trezor says it reviewed each country on its own, weighing revenue and distribution against its own presence there, and that resellers who stay will face an updated legal framework and tighter rules on how devices are sourced, stored, and handled.
Trezor said on X earlier this week that CryptoBilis was already off its seller list and that it had received no reports of tampered Trezors from the retailer.

We are actively investigating the…

In May 2022, Trezor warned that counterfeit Model T wallets were being sold on a Russian marketplace by a seller that was not an authorized reseller. The devices had been opened, resealed, and fitted with replaced internal components, and Trezor said the recovery phrases they generated were predictable or predefined, meaning someone else could already know the words.
Trezor's advice then was to buy only from its official shop or an authorized reseller. The second option is the network it is now shrinking.
In August, shipping partner ShipMonk exposed Trezor customer data after unauthorized access, and Trezor's September update put the total at 80,689 customers. Trezor says its systems, devices, private keys, and wallet backups were not affected.
Ledger told anyone who bought from CryptoBilis in the past 90 days not to set up their device, and told those who already did to move their funds to a new seed phrase on a device bought from Ledger. Ledger and Trezor have each warned buyers against unauthorized sellers.

title: AI Powered PlayStation Crack Could Let You Play GTA 6 on PC at Launch - Decrypt
text:
Vibe coders are porting PlayStation 5 applications to Windows and Linux, leaving some users optimistic that the project will unlock better performance for PS5 games, and could even work for GTA 6 at launch.
AnyPS5 is an open-source, AI-powered project on GitHub that converts PS5 game executables into programs that run natively on PC, swapping Sony’s system libraries for its own version rather than emulating the console. A community-run tracker lists more than 180 PS5 titles that have been tried with the tool, but only a handful have been verified as playable.
An important distinction to make is that this is not an emulator and that games will be running natively on PC. As a result, some speculators believe that users will be able to get better performance from PS5 games by playing them on a high-powered PC.
"GTA 6 most likely will be able to run on your PC at launch, and [with] significantly higher frames than it would on your PS5," pseudonymous gaming content creator Schlayerr said on TikTok. "We live in a crazy time."
"Technically, this is feasible given the similarities between console and PC architectures, and AI can dramatically accelerate the reverse engineering work," Theodore Agranat, Director of Web3 at Gunzilla Games, the game studio behind battle royale Off the Grid, told Decrypt. However, he remained skeptical over whether they "can deliver the quality, performance, and fidelity players expect from AAA games at scale."

Development has been FAST since Friday, and the library side is becoming the next phase to watch.

— Chris Mizo (@MizoChris) October 12, 2026
The latest project update claims that 100% of the PS5 GPU shaders have been ported while 88% of the system libraries have been ported. Discord community members believe the final 12% for system libraries is likely to take a long time, especially as new system libraries are continuously being discovered.
In the Discord showcase channel, some users have shown off rudimentary demos of PS5 games on PC. One community developer reported running GTA 5 at 27 frames per second, or FPS, in the performance graphics mode. Others have reported getting 4 FPS on Epic Mickey, 25 FPS on Phasmophobia, and 60 FPS on Vampire Survivors. It's still a work in progress.
Still, in all of these examples, the games aren't fully playable due to the incomplete system library port as well as game-specific bugs being encountered.
A potential roadblock in playing GTA 6 on PC at launch is a mandatory firmware update, Discord members say. This is because the AnyPS5 project would need to overhaul its converted files to the latest update in order to get GTA 6 running. As such, there is likely to be a delay before the game is available on PC via AnyPS5.
"Firmware updates could create hurdles, particularly around DRM, but likely wouldn’t invalidate the entire approach," Agranat said.
AnyPS5 bans any form of piracy in its Discord server, meaning using the tool requires purchasing the game on the PlayStation Store. That said, there is nothing stopping an individual using AnyPS5 with a pirated copy of a video game.
Some PlayStation users have speculated that the movement is a response to Sony's plan to discontinue physical game discs.
"The reason this all happened is because Sony discontinued discs," pseudonymous gaming content creator The 1st Gamer said on TikTok. "They wanted to go digital, and they did, but just not on PS5."
Sony announced in July that it plans to stop producing physical discs at the start of 2028. The decision was met with major community backlash, including a petition called "Don't Kill the Disc" gaining over 385,000 signatures. Shawn Layden, a former PlayStation executive, called the move a "heavily spreadsheeted decision" and said it has damaged the company's reputation.
In August, Sony argued in a California court that purchasing a digital game in the PlayStation Store does not equate to ownership of it. Sony claimed its Terms of Service and the Software Product License Agreement explain this and that users should understand it as a fact.
"Even without Sony stopping physical discs, this was bound to happen with AI accelerating dev," Agrant said. "My hope is that projects like this push platform holders to offer the same flexibility themselves, but at a much higher standard," he told Decrypt, hoping for a future where Sony rolls out games on PC as well as console. "That would be a genuine win-win."

title: Ledger Finds LTE Implant That Stole Recovery Phrases in Suspected $86M Drain - Decrypt
text:
Ledger said its security research team has found an unauthorized hardware implant that captured recovery phrases inside wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, in a tweet on Tuesday.
The Paris-based hardware wallet manufacturer said it confirmed the implant on Saturday in one affected user's device. All confirmed losses from the incident, which Ledger disclosed on Friday, involve devices sold through CryptoBilis, and the company said it has not verified a drain linked to a device bought elsewhere.
Update from Ledger Donjon on the CryptoBilis investigation 🔽@DonjonLedger is investigating Ledger signers sold by CryptoBilis, a reseller in Southeast Asia, that contained an unauthorized hardware implant. Ledger confirmed this on October 10th for one affected user's signer.…
— Ledger (@Ledger) October 13, 2026
A Ledger device, which the company calls a signer, shows a 24-word recovery phrase during setup. Anyone holding that phrase can restore the wallet and control its funds.
According to the analysis by Ledger Donjon, the company's security team, the implant sits inside the device's enclosure and reads what is shown on the screen. When it detects the recovery phrase screens, its microcontroller decodes the words and transmits them over LTE using a provisioned eSIM.
The implant is a separate component, Ledger said, adding that it does not modify the device's Secure Element or the Ledger operating system, nor does it alter transactions or signatures.
CryptoBilis has confirmed it stopped selling Ledger devices while the investigation continues, according to Ledger.
Ledger said it has not confirmed the total number of affected users or the value lost, and that figures circulating online come from third parties it has not fully verified. Onchain investigator Specter traced more than $86 million in suspected thefts across Ethereum, Tron and Bitcoin, Decrypt reported on Friday.
Ledger said it is also reviewing reports of implants in other signers and locations. An X user has claimed to have found two tampered Ledger devices bought from retail stores in Europe, a claim that has not been independently verified.
The company told CryptoBilis buyers who have not set up their device not to do so and to contact Ledger Support. Those who have should move their assets promptly to a new device with a new recovery phrase, and should not enter or restore any recovery phrase on a device bought from CryptoBilis.
Users who lost funds or hold a tampered device should also file a report with local law enforcement, Ledger said, and should not send the device to anyone, or open it, before speaking to Ledger Support or the police.
Buyers who did not purchase from CryptoBilis can inspect the inside of their device using a Ledger guide, though the company warned that opening a signer can damage it and urged users to back up their recovery phrase first.
Ledger reiterated that it will never call users, message them directly or ask for their recovery phrase. The Donjon will analyze the devices it receives and share more as the investigation continues, the company said.

title: UK Moves Closer to Keeping $5B Bitcoin Haul After High Court Ruling - Decrypt
text:
The UK government's chances of keeping a 61,000 BTC haul seized from convicted fraudster Zhimin Qian have improved after the High Court in London ruled on Monday that Chinese law should govern victims' claims to the coins.
The Bitcoin is worth about $5 billion at its current price of around $83,200, per CoinGecko data.
Qian was jailed for more than 11 years last year after pleading guilty to fraud and money laundering charges over a Ponzi scheme that defrauded investors in China between 2014 and 2017. According to the ruling, at least 128,409 investment contracts were entered into, and victims paid in about RMB 40.2 billion, roughly £4.1 billion. About RMB 34.1 billion of that was paid back out to some victims.
Thousands of victims have applied under the Proceeds of Crime Act to have parts of the Bitcoin declared theirs. To succeed, each must show a proprietary interest in the coins, Justice Mark Turner wrote, because the law creates no broader compensation scheme for people who lost out to crime.
English law had been seen as substantially more favorable to the victims, the Financial Times reported, because it could have let them argue the Bitcoin belonged to them.
Turner sided with the Director of Public Prosecutions, who heads the Crown Prosecution Service and brought the case, finding that the fraud, the victims' payments and the contracts all took place in China. "The relevant damage occurred in China. The Applicants parted with their money in China," he wrote.
The judge reached the same answer under each of the legal routes he considered, concluding that the governing law "is Chinese law." Because the Bitcoin was bought in China, he added, tracing the coins in England cannot revive any property rights the victims lost under Chinese law when that purchase took place.
The decision does not settle who keeps the Bitcoin. Questions about the content and proof of Chinese law are matters for a later stage, Turner wrote. Prosecutors have previously said victims could be compensated through a redress scheme run from China.
Unnamed Treasury officials have privately raised whether the seized Bitcoin, worth around $7 billion at the time of Qian's trial, could help fill a shortfall in the UK's public finances, the FT reported last year.
Law firm Fieldfisher, which represents the claimants, said it is pursuing an appeal, according to the FT. "There will be a further hearing to determine the application of the law and if any of the victims are able to establish an interest in the bitcoin," the CPS said.

title: ‘Leave’: Crypto Backlash Over French Proposal to Report Wallets Over $112K - Decrypt
text:
Lawmakers in France have advanced a proposal that will require crypto holders to report holdings equal to or above €100,000 ($112,000). Otherwise, individuals will face fines up to €10,000 ($11,000).
Some crypto holders are in an uproar over the potential new rule, claiming that it threatens personal security. It comes after several high-profile, in-person crypto robberies have taken place in France.
"This is a terrible idea as corrupt employees in the French tax authority have has already shown themselves to a danger to their own citizens," Harry Halpin, CEO of privacy infrastructure Nym, told Decrypt, referencing a recent case in which a French tax agent was accused of selling data from the French tax authority to criminals.
France should be "held accountable" to victims of crypto kidnappings, Halpin continued. "In the future, criminals will use chain analytics and other AI surveillance," he said, adding that, "The only solution to defend your data and cryptocurrency is to use shielded cryptocurrency like Zcash and actually private VPNs."
This is the same government whose employees sold tax returns of crypto holders to criminals. If you live in france and hold crypto, leave. If you cant leave, hire personal security for you and your family. https://t.co/DKEmJ7S1Fy
— Rand (@randhindi) October 12, 2026
The French National Assembly's Finance Committee adopted the amendment I-CF821 on Friday, which would introduce reporting requirements for crypto assets held in a self-custody wallet. In a self-custody wallet, the owner holds private keys that allow them to fully control the assets inside it, in contrast to non-custodial ownership platforms like centralized exchanges.
The proposal would see a provision added to France's general tax code requiring crypto users to declare holdings equal to or above €100,000 ($112,000), based on the value at the end of the calendar year.
It is important to note that the proposed rule is not law yet and is subject to change.
"If you live in France and hold crypto, leave," Rand Hindi, founder of privacy protocol Zama, tweeted. "If you can't leave, hire personal security for you and your family."
According to the amendment, the new rule is to fight against using cryptocurrency as a vector for fraud, as it claims that crypto ownership is underestimated.
France has emerged as a hotspot for crypto robberies in recent years.
In 2025, Ledger co-founder David Balland and his wife were kidnapped from their home and held for ransom in a wrench attack that saw one of Balland's fingers severed by the attackers. Earlier this year, the wife of Sébastien Borget, The Sandbox co-founder, was the victim of an attempted kidnapping at her home in Villenoy, Seine-et-Marne. A couple in their late 50s were forced to transfer $1 million in Bitcoin at knifepoint by robbers pretending to be police in Versailles, France, earlier this year.
This troubling trend is a major reason that crypto participants feel apprehensive about declaring their holdings.
"France is the leading country on the planet for crypto kidnappings and wrench attacks," Mert Mumtaz, CEO of Solana-based infrastructure firm Helius, tweeted. "Now they want to increase by 50,000x the amount of data they collect and hence leak."
It’s not the only crypto measure the committee waved through last week. It also voted to treat swaps from crypto into stablecoins as taxable sales from January 2027, and to extend France’s exit tax to crypto held by households worth more than €800,000.
But the committee then rejected the budget’s entire revenue section, 31 votes to 3. The full National Assembly now starts from the government’s original text, which doesn’t include any of the crypto amendments, when the floor debate resumes on Monday. If lawmakers want them back, they’ll have to table them again.
